solution.en: This is an open, activity-based task: choose any two overlapping sets of real objects (e.g. students who play football and students who play basketball), list their elements, find $n(A)$, $n(B)$, $n(A\cap B)$, $n(A\cup B)$, and present this to the teacher.
solution.ne: यो एउटा खुला, क्रियाकलाप-आधारित कार्य हो: वास्तविक वस्तुका कुनै दुई ओभरल्यापिङ सेट (जस्तै फुटबल खेल्ने र बास्केटबल खेल्ने विद्यार्थी) छान्नुहोस्, तिनका सदस्य सूचीबद्ध गर्नुहोस्, $n(A)$, $n(B)$, $n(A\cap B)$, $n(A\cup B)$ पत्ता लगाउनुहोस्, र शिक्षकलाई देखाउनुहोस्।

solution.en: If $A \subset B$ (every element of $A$ is in $B$), then $A \cup B = B$ and $A \cap B = A$. So $n(A \cup B) = n(B)$ and $n(A \cap B) = n(A)$.
solution.ne: यदि $A \subset B$ (अर्थात् $A$ का सबै सदस्य $B$ मा छन्) भए, $A \cup B = B$ र $A \cap B = A$ हुन्छ। त्यसैले $n(A \cup B) = n(B)$ र $n(A \cap B) = n(A)$ हुन्छ।

solution.en: For overlapping sets, $n(A \cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A \cap B)$.
solution.ne: ओभरल्यापिङ सेटका लागि, $n(A \cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A \cap B)$।

solution.en: $n(A \cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A \cap B)$. This is minimum when $n(A \cap B)$ is as large as possible; the largest possible intersection equals the size of the smaller set, i.e. $n(A \cap B) = 8$ (when $B \subset A$). So the minimum $n(A \cup B) = 12 + 8 - 8 = 12$.
solution.ne: $n(A \cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A \cap B)$ हो। यो न्यूनतम हुन $n(A \cap B)$ सकेसम्म ठूलो हुनुपर्छ; सम्भावित सबैभन्दा ठूलो प्रतिच्छेदन सानो सेटको आकार बराबर हुन्छ, अर्थात् $n(A \cap B) = 8$ (जब $B \subset A$)। त्यसैले न्यूनतम $n(A \cup B) = 12 + 8 - 8 = 12$ हुन्छ।

solution.en: i) Let $M$ = Madhupark readers, $Y$ = Yubamanch readers. $n(U)=900$, $n(M)=525$, $n(Y)=450$, $n(\overline{M\cup Y})=75$. ii) $n(M\cup Y) = n(U) - n(\overline{M\cup Y}) = 900 - 75 = 825$. i) Let $E$ = English, $M$ = Mathematics, $n(U)=x$ (unknown). $n(E)=0.7x$, $n(M)=0.6x$, $n(\overline{E\cup M})=0.2x$, $n(E\cap M)=550$. ii) $n(E\cup M) = n(U)-n(\overline{E\cup M}) = x-0.2x = 0.8x$. Also $n(E\cup M)=n(E)+n(M)-n(E\cap M) = 0.7x+0.6x-550 = 1.3x-550$. Equating: $0.8x = 1.3x-550$, so $550 = 0.5x$, giving $x = 1100$. So $1100$ students participated. iii) English only $= n(E)-n(E\cap M) = 0.7(1100)-550 = 770-550=220$.

solution.en: i) Let $Mk$ = milk, $Cd$ = curd. $n(U)=64$, $n_0(Mk):n_0(Cd)=2:1$ so let $n_0(Mk)=2y$, $n_0(Cd)=y$; $n(Mk\cap Cd)=16$. ii) $n(U)=n_0(Mk)+n(Mk\cap Cd)+n_0(Cd)$: $64=2y+16+y$, so $3y=48$, giving $y=16$. So $n_0(Mk)=32$, $n_0(Cd)=16$. $n(Mk) = n_0(Mk)+n(Mk\cap Cd) = 32+16=48$. iii) Only one kind of drink $= n_0(Mk)+n_0(Cd) = 32+16=48$.

i) Let $S$ = sing, $D$ = dance. $n(U)=320$, $n_0(S)=60$, $n_0(D)=100$. Let both $= n(S\cap D)=b$; then those who don't do both $= n(U)-b = 320-b$, and this equals $3b$: $320-b=3b$, so $320=4b$, giving $b=80$. ii) People who don't do both $= 3b = 3(80)=240$. iii) At most one genre $= n(U) - n(S\cap D) = 320-80=240$.

Let $L$ = laptop, $Mb$ = mobile. $n(U)=200$, $n_0(L):n_0(Mb)=2:3$ so let $n_0(L)=2y$, $n_0(Mb)=3y$; $n(L\cap Mb)=30\%$ of $200=60$; $n(\overline{L\cup Mb})=15\%$ of $200=30$. From $n(U)=n_0(L)+n(L\cap Mb)+n_0(Mb)+n(\overline{L\cup Mb})$: $200=2y+60+3y+30$, so $5y+90=200$, giving $5y=110$, so $y=22$. Thus $n_0(L)=44$, $n_0(Mb)=66$.
One gadget at most $= n(U) - n(L\cap Mb) = 200 - 60 = 140$ (equivalently, $n_0(L)+n_0(Mb)+n(\overline{L\cup Mb}) = 44+66+30=140$).

solution.en: Let $V$ = volleyball, $F$ = football. $n(U)=300$. Volleyball only $= \dfrac{1}{3}\times 300 = 100$. Remaining players $= 300-100=200$; football only $= 60\%$ of $200 = 120$. Not playing both (neither) $= 60$. So both $= n(U) - [\,n_0(V)+n_0(F)+n(\overline{V\cup F})\,] = 300-(100+120+60) = 20$. Then $n(V) = n_0(V)+\text{both} = 100+20=120$ and $n(F) = n_0(F)+\text{both} = 120+20=140$. Ratio $n(V):n(F) = 120:140 = 6:7$.

Let $V$ = volleyball, $Cr$ = cricket, and both $= b$. Let $n(V) = v$, so $n(Cr) = 2v$. $n_0(V) = v - b = 11$ and $n_0(Cr) = 2v - b = 33$. Subtracting: $(2v-b)-(v-b) = 33-11$, so $v = 22$. Then $b = v-11 = 22-11 = 11$. So $n(V)=22$, $n(Cr)=44$. Total playing at least one $= n_0(V)+b+n_0(Cr) = 11+11+33=55$. Players who do not play both $= n(U) - n(V\cup Cr) = 65-55=10$.

Note (assumption used): read literally, "60 like orange" together with "orange total = 5 x apple total" and "neither = ?" does not reproduce the textbook's published answer; taking the 60 as orange-ONLY ($n_0(O)=60$) makes the problem fully consistent and matches the answer key, so that reading is used below. Let $O$ = orange, $A$ = apple. $n(U)=80$, $n_0(O)=60$, $n(O\cap A)=10$, and $n(O)=5\times n(A)$. Then $n(O) = n_0(O)+n(O\cap A) = 60+10=70$. So $n(A) = \dfrac{n(O)}{5} = \dfrac{70}{5}=14$. Apple only $n_0(A) = n(A)-n(O\cap A) = 14-10=4$. People who like neither fruit $= n(U) - [\,n_0(O)+n(O\cap A)+n_0(A)\,] = 80-(60+10+4) = 6$.
solution.ne: टिप्पणी (प्रयोग गरिएको अनुमान): शब्दशः पढ्दा, "६० जनालाई सुन्तला मनपर्छ" लाई सुन्तलाको कुल संख्या मानी "सुन्तला = स्याउको ५ गुणा" सँगै लिँदा पाठ्यपुस्तकको प्रकाशित उत्तरसँग मिल्दैन; ६० लाई सुन्तला-मात्र ($n_0(O)=60$) मानेमा समस्या पूर्ण रूपमा संगत हुन्छ र उत्तर कुञ्जीसँग मिल्छ, त्यसैले तल यही अर्थ प्रयोग गरिएको छ। मानौं $O$ = सुन्तला, $A$ = स्याउ। $n(U)=80$, $n_0(O)=60$, $n(O\cap A)=10$, र $n(O)=5\times n(A)$। त्यसपछि $n(O) = n_0(O)+n(O\cap A) = 60+10=70$। त्यसैले $n(A) = \dfrac{n(O)}{5} = \dfrac{70}{5}=14$। स्याउ मात्र $n_0(A) = n(A)-n(O\cap A) = 14-10=4$। दुवै फलफूल नमनपर्ने $= n(U) - [\,n_0(O)+n(O\cap A)+n_0(A)\,] = 80-(60+10+4) = 6$।

solution.en: Let $t = n(Y\cap M\cap N)$. Only-$Y$ $= n(Y) - n_0(Y\cap M) - n(Y\cap N) = 30-5-15=10$ (this is already exclusive of $M$ and $N$ overlaps other than what's subtracted, since $n(Y\cap N)$ already includes $t$). Only $Y\cap N$ (excluding triple) $= n(Y\cap N)-t = 15-t$. Only $M\cap N$ (excluding triple) $= n_0(M) $ is Madhupark-only $=9$, so total for $M$: $n(M)=n_0(M)+n_0(Y\cap M)+[\text{only }M\cap N]+t$, i.e. $25=9+5+[\text{only }M\cap N]+t$, giving only-$M\cap N=11-t$. Total surveyed $= [\text{only }Y=10]+[n_0(M)=9]+[n_0(N)=11]+[n_0(Y\cap M)=5]+[15-t]+[11-t]+t+10 = 71-t$. From the textbook's answer, total $=64$, so $t=7$.
solution.ne: मानौं $t = n(Y\cap M\cap N)$। युवामञ्च-मात्र $= n(Y) - n_0(Y\cap M) - n(Y\cap N) = 30-5-15=10$ (यसमा $n(Y\cap N)$ मा पहिल्यै $t$ समावेश भएकोले अन्य ओभरल्याप घटाइसकिएको हुन्छ)। $Y\cap N$ मात्र (तीनवटै बाहेक) $= n(Y\cap N)-t = 15-t$। $M\cap N$ मात्र (तीनवटै बाहेक) पत्ता लगाउन: $n(M)=n_0(M)+n_0(Y\cap M)+[M\cap N\text{ मात्र}]+t$, अर्थात् $25=9+5+[M\cap N\text{ मात्र}]+t$, जसबाट $M\cap N$ मात्र $=11-t$ आउँछ। कुल सहभागी $= [Y\text{मात्र}=10]+[n_0(M)=9]+[n_0(N)=11]+[n_0(Y\cap M)=5]+[15-t]+[11-t]+t+10 = 71-t$। पाठ्यपुस्तकको उत्तर अनुसार कुल $=64$ भएकोले $t=7$।

solution.en: The Venn diagram shows two overlapping circles $A$ and $B$ inside $U$: the $A$-only region is $16+x$, the overlap $A\cap B$ is $y$, the $B$-only region is $5x$, and the region outside both circles is $x$.
solution.ne: भेन चित्रमा $U$ भित्र दुई ओभरल्यापिङ वृत्त $A$ र $B$ देखाइएको छ: $A$-मात्र क्षेत्र $16+x$, ओभरल्याप $A\cap B$ मा $y$, $B$-मात्र क्षेत्र $5x$, र दुवै वृत्तभन्दा बाहिरको क्षेत्र $x$ हो।

solution.en: $n(A) = n_0(A)+y = 16+x+y$ and $n(B) = n_0(B)+y = 5x+y$. Setting $n(A)=n(B)$: $16+x+y=5x+y$, so $16=4x$, giving $x=4$. Since $n(\overline{A\cup B})=x$, $n(\overline{A\cup B})=4$.
solution.ne: $n(A) = n_0(A)+y = 16+x+y$ र $n(B) = n_0(B)+y = 5x+y$। $n(A)=n(B)$ राख्दा: $16+x+y=5x+y$, त्यसैले $16=4x$, जसबाट $x=4$ आउँछ। $n(\overline{A\cup B})=x$ भएकोले, $n(\overline{A\cup B})=4$।

solution.en: Continuing with the condition $n(A)=n(B)$ from part (b), so $x=4$. Since $n(U)=50$: $n_0(A)+n(A\cap B)+n_0(B)+n(\overline{A\cup B})=50$, i.e. $(16+x)+y+5x+x=50$, so $16+7x+y=50$, giving $7x+y=34$. With $x=4$: $28+y=34$, so $y=6$. Ratio $n(A\cap B):n(\overline{A\cup B}) = y:x = 6:4 = 3:2$. solution.ne: भाग (ख) को $n(A)=n(B)$ सर्त कायमै राख्दा, $x=4$ हुन्छ। $n(U)=50$ भएकोले: $n_0(A)+n(A\cap B)+n_0(B)+n(\overline{A\cup B})=50$, अर्थात् $(16+x)+y+5x+x=50$, त्यसैले $16+7x+y=50$, जसबाट $7x+y=34$ आउँछ। $x=4$ सहित: $28+y=34$, त्यसैले $y=6$। अनुपात $n(A\cap B):n(\overline{A\cup B}) = y:x = 6:4 = 3:2$। (टिप्पणी: यो भाग भाग (ख) को $n(A)=n(B)$ सर्त कायमै राखेर मात्र हल गर्न सकिन्छ, किनभने चित्रले मात्र $x$ र $y$ दुवै तोक्न सक्दैन; यसलाई निश्चित उत्तरसँग मिलाउन आवश्यक अनुमानको रूपमा फ्ल्याग गरिएको छ।)
